paras.text: There can be several possible methods for the solution of problems. Every method has disadvantages and advantages. Now the best solution to the problem is to choose the best among several possible methods. For this it is necessary that every method be stated and the strengths and weaknesses of each be reviewed. For this, information is collected by those same methods, i.e. observation, interview, questionnaire, books and the internet etc. are used to obtain information, and after arrangement and study the causes of this problem, its results and possible solutions become known. For example, one possible solution is the provision of employment. If people are given opportunities of employment, poverty can be reduced. The advantages of this solution are that people will become able to earn and will be able to bring comfort into their lives. Business can be started by collecting a small capital. Through employment the country also progresses, and unemployment decreasing, crimes too will decrease. For the government too the difficulties will decrease. Opportunities of employment will be more, and trained manpower will be available in the country. Methods to Solve Problems in the Light of Information

There can be several possible methods for the solution of problems. Every method has disadvantages and advantages. Now the best solution to the problem is to choose the best among several possible methods. For this it is necessary that every method be stated and the strengths and weaknesses of each be reviewed. For example, take the problem of “poverty”. Now the causes of poverty, its results and the methods of controlling it have to be found. For this, information is collected by those same methods, i.e. observation, interview, questionnaire, books and the internet etc. are used to obtain information, and after arrangement and study the causes of this problem, its results and possible solutions become known. For example, one possible solution is the provision of employment. If people are given opportunities of employment, poverty can be reduced. The advantages of this solution are that people will become able to earn and will be able to bring comfort into their lives. Business can be started by collecting a small capital. Through employment the country also progresses, and unemployment decreasing, crimes too will decrease. For the government too the difficulties will decrease. This solution also has weaknesses, i.e. where will the government create opportunities of employment from immediately? How will the government determine priorities in the provision of employment? In it there can be nepotism, corruption and several kinds of prejudices at work. The second way of ending poverty is to control population. The advantages of this solution will be that by controlling population there will be no burden on resources and the possibilities of poverty will decrease. With planning, when children are born, their upbringing and training will be easy, and good healthy nations will be formed. Opportunities of employment will be more, and trained manpower will be available in the country. paras.text: … programme will be needed, on which considerable expense will also come. It is possible that despite efforts and expense the increase in population cannot be stopped. The third solution is the establishment of industries. If industries are set up, then on one side the country will progress and on the other side people will have income. Along with this, small businesses too will arise. Among people the inclination to obtain technical education will increase. Expert manpower will increase. On the other side, the weaknesses are where the government will get the money from, how it will set up so many factories. Loans will be taken from world institutions, making the country further indebted, and in the beginning how will technical training be given to people? Another way is that people be sent abroad. Its advantages will be that money will come into the country from outside. The public will also benefit financially. More capital will come in hand with less labour. Investment can be made here with that money and in this way sustainable development can start. The disadvantages of this solution are that the government will have to make agreements with other countries, which is a laborious and difficult work. People are not experts, therefore they have to do labour work abroad too, which is not easy. Where will the money come from to send people abroad; this too is an issue. The third solution is the establishment of industries. If industries are set up, then on one side the country will progress and on the other side people will have income. Along with this, small businesses too will arise. Among people the inclination to obtain technical education will increase. Expert manpower will increase. On the other side, the weaknesses are where the government will get the money from, how it will set up so many factories. Loans will be taken from world institutions, making the country further indebted, and in the beginning how will technical training be given to people? Another way is that people be sent abroad. Its advantages will be that money will come into the country from outside. The public will also benefit financially. More capital will come in hand with less labour. Investment can be made here with that money and in this way sustainable development can start. The disadvantages of this solution are that the government will have to make agreements with other countries, which is a laborious and difficult work. People are not experts, therefore they have to do labour work abroad too, which is not easy. Where will the money come from to send people abroad; this too is an issue. Most people, because of ignorance, do such works abroad which also become the cause of the country’s bad name.

On the basis of information the researcher becomes able to give the government proposals for suitable policy or law-making, which is called a policy paper. The government too needs such ideal and positive proposals. The step-by-step method of preparing a policy paper is somewhat like this:

1. Identification of the problem (what is the problem).

2. Three or four possible solutions of the problem.

3. What are the prominent advantages and disadvantages of every possible solution.

4. Recommendation of the best solution.

… programme will be needed, on which considerable expense will also come. It is possible that despite efforts and expense the increase in population cannot be stopped. The third solution is the establishment of industries. If industries are set up, then on one side the country will progress and on the other side people will have income. Along with this, small businesses too will arise. Among people the inclination to obtain technical education will increase. Expert manpower will increase. On the other side, the weaknesses are where the government will get the money from, how it will set up so many factories. Loans will be taken from world institutions, making the country further indebted, and in the beginning how will technical training be given to people? Another way is that people be sent abroad. Its advantages will be that money will come into the country from outside. The public will also benefit financially. More capital will come in hand with less labour. Investment can be made here with that money and in this way sustainable development can start. The disadvantages of this solution are that the government will have to make agreements with other countries, which is a laborious and difficult work. People are not experts, therefore they have to do labour work abroad too, which is not easy. Where will the money come from to send people abroad; this too is an issue. Most people, because of ignorance, do such works abroad which also become the cause of the country’s bad name.

Now, of the said methods, either one solution or several solutions together, a suitable and practicable method can be adopted. But every matter will have to be seen from every angle, so that the most work can be done easily at the least expense.

Proposal To Make Government Policy to Solve Problems

On the basis of information the researcher becomes able to give the government proposals for suitable policy or law-making, which is called a policy paper. The government too needs such ideal and positive proposals. The step-by-step method of preparing a policy paper is somewhat like this:

1. Identification of the problem (what is the problem).

2. Three or four possible solutions of the problem.

3. What are the prominent advantages and disadvantages of every possible solution.

4. Recommendation of the best solution.
